tasks.title: P29-01 — D96 + D100: the persisted write and its parameters — one transaction over one declaration
tasks.description: Two stores, one rule: a persisted write either applies exactly its declared parameters atomically or leaves the rows untouched. In `StudyStore.save`, build the serialized row list BEFORE any connection use (`rows = [(symbol, study["type"], 1 if study.get("enabled") else 0, json.dumps(deepcopy(study.get("params", {})))) for study in studies]`), then run the `DELETE` and the `executemany` inside `with db.conn:` and remove the trailing `db.conn.commit()`; the original `TypeError`/`IntegrityError`/`OperationalError` surfaces unwrapped, once. In `DrawingStore.update_group`, reject `set(fields) - {"name","color","visible","locked"}` with `ValueError(f"update_group: unknown field(s): {', '.join(unknown)}")` BEFORE `db.conn.cursor()`, then build one `pairs = [(k, v) for k, v in fields.items() if k in allowed]` list and derive `assigns` and `values` from it — bool->int only for `visible`/`locked`, a bool supplied for `name`/`color` raises `ValueError(f"update_group: {key} expects a string, got bool")`, and empty `fields` stays the today's no-op. Write the new suite `tests/test_d96_d100_store_atomicity.py` (shared temp DB from conftest, one dedicated symbol, fixtures committed before each call). Do not add a helper module, a second connection, an explicit BEGIN/ROLLBACK, a retry/queue, a new exception type, or any change to the studies/drawing_groups DDL, `load`, `sanitize_study_params`, or any other store method; the three `update_group` call sites in `ui/drawing_groups_dialog.py` are AUDITED (each passes one allowed key) and not edited.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a symbol with stored studies, When `StudyStore.save` raises for EITHER failure class — a non-serializable param (`TypeError` from `json.dumps`) or a forced DB error between the DELETE and the INSERT (`sqlite3.IntegrityError` from `type=None` against `studies.type NOT NULL`) — Then `load(symbol)` is byte-identical to before (json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True) comparison), `db.conn.in_transaction is False` immediately after the call, and `load(symbol)` is still byte-identical after an unrelated write + commit on the same connection; and a subsequent valid `save` succeeds and leaves exactly the valid set.

Given a valid study set, When `save` returns, Then the store holds exactly that set — row count and `load` equality — and two successive saves leave exactly the second set (replace-all semantics unchanged).
Given an empty list, When `save(symbol, [])` runs, Then the symbol's rows are removed and committed (`load(symbol) == []`, `db.conn.in_transaction is False`).

Given an update whose `fields` contain at least one key outside {"name","color","visible","locked"}, When `update_group` runs, Then a `ValueError` naming every unknown key is raised before a cursor exists — a `db.conn.set_trace_callback` installed before the call records ZERO statements — the group row is unchanged, `in_transaction` is False, and both stay true after an unrelated commit.

Given any subset of the four allowed fields (including two at once and the empty subset), When `update_group` runs, Then exactly those columns change and the others are untouched, the empty subset is a no-op, and every UPDATE statement the trace records binds exactly as many parameters as it has placeholders.

Given a boolean value supplied for a column, When `update_group` runs, Then `visible`/`locked` coerce bool to int and read back as True/False, while a bool supplied for `name` or `color` raises `ValueError` and changes nothing.

tests.description: Two committed studies for a dedicated symbol; `save` with `params={"bad": object()}`; then an unrelated write + `commit()`.
tests.expected_result: `TypeError` surfaces once; `load` is byte-identical before/after and again after the unrelated commit; `db.conn.in_transaction is False` right after the failing call.

tests.description: A committed study set; `save` with `type=None` (forces `IntegrityError` between DELETE and INSERT); then an unrelated write + `commit()`.
tests.expected_result: `sqlite3.IntegrityError` surfaces; rows byte-identical immediately and after the unrelated commit; `in_transaction is False` right after the failure.

tests.description: First-write-on-connection variant: assert `in_transaction is False` immediately before the failing call, on a connection whose only prior writes were committed fixture seeds; then retry with a valid set.
tests.expected_result: No transaction is open before the call or after the failure, the seeded prior set survives, and the retry stores exactly the valid set.

tests.description: Parametrized over one valid set and two successive valid sets for the same symbol.
tests.expected_result: Row count equals the stored set's length, `load` returns exactly it, and after the second save only the second set is present.

tests.description: Two committed studies, then `save(symbol, [])`.
tests.expected_result: `load(symbol) == []` and `db.conn.in_transaction is False` (the empty set is committed, not left pending).

tests.description: `set_trace_callback(records.append)` cleared before the call; parametrized over `{"visible": False, "bogus": 1}` and `{"bogus": 1}` alone; repeated after an unrelated commit; callback removed in `finally`.
tests.expected_result: `ValueError` message names `bogus`; `records == []` (no SQL at all); the group row is unchanged; `in_transaction is False`, before and after the unrelated commit.

tests.description: Parametrized over `{"visible": False}`, `{"visible": False, "locked": True}`, `{"color": "#123456"}`, `{"name": "renamed"}` and `{}`.
tests.expected_result: Exactly the named columns change (others read back unchanged); `{}` returns without raising and changes nothing; the trace shows one UPDATE whose bound-parameter count equals its placeholder count.

tests.description: `visible=True` then read-back; `name=True` and `color=True` each attempted with the trace callback installed.
tests.expected_result: `visible` stores 1 and reads back `True`; each bool-for-text call raises `ValueError`, records no statement, and leaves the row unchanged.

tasks.title: P29-02 — D97: one crossing rule, previous side inclusive
tasks.description: Replace `evaluate_alarms`'s two strict comparisons with the phase's one rule: `crossed_above = prev_price <= alarm.price < curr_price` and `crossed_below = prev_price >= alarm.price > curr_price`. The previous-side boundary is INCLUSIVE (a touch arms), the current-side boundary is EXCLUSIVE (sitting on the level never fires), and a touch is derived — DG133 — so NO alarm field is added. Every other line of the function (the `prev_price is None or curr_price <= 0` guard, the kind/active/triggered skips, the `cross_either` disjunction, the signature and return type) stays byte-identical, and the docstring gains the rule stated once. In `tests/test_alarm_service.py`, re-baseline exactly ONE named case: `TestBoundaryAndState::test_exactly_on_alert_price_above_counts` (9.5 -> 10.0 currently fires) becomes `test_arrival_on_the_level_is_a_touch_not_a_cross` — `evaluate_alarms(9.5, 10.0, [alarm@10.0 cross_above]) == []`, then `evaluate_alarms(10.0, 10.01, [fresh same-level alarm]) == [alarm]` — with `AC-D97.1`/A242 cited in its docstring. `test_equal_prev_price_is_not_a_cross` already encodes the new rule and stays unmodified; add the Journey 79 edge cases in the same file. Do not add an Alarm field, a cache, a clock or a second evaluation path, and do not change `evaluate_volume_burst`, `_resolve_z_threshold`, `TickerSession._on_aggregated_bar`, or any other shipped case.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an alarm whose level equals the current sample, When subsequent samples are evaluated, Then a sample that stays at the level does not fire, the first sample strictly beyond the level in the alarm's direction fires exactly once, and any further sample beyond does not fire (the `triggered` latch) — for `cross_above`, `cross_below` and `cross_either`.

Given a seed tick (`prev_price is None`) at exactly the level, Then no alarm fires on the seed for any of the three directions, and a non-positive current price still returns [] (the AC-D25.3 guard stays green).
Given a `cross_above` alarm touched at the level, When the next sample is strictly below the level, Then it does not fire; and the mirror for `cross_below` touched then crossed upward.

Given the shipped pure function, Then its signature, its `prev is None or curr_price <= 0` guard, its inactive/already-triggered skips and its return type are unchanged; a one-tick gap over the level fires (9.0 -> 11.0); a return to the level after firing does not re-fire; and `Alarm` still carries no touch/armed field.

tests.expected_result: Neither directional alarm fires on the opposite-direction move.

tasks.title: P29-03 — D98: one outage baseline, one resume path, and a failed launch is not an outage
tasks.description: Any outage behaves like the TWS-gone outage for evaluation: the first post-outage tick seeds, the unmonitored interval is reported. Add `AlarmMonitor.begin_outage()` — it RETURNS IMMEDIATELY when `self._host._sessions` is empty (a failed/pre-handshake `connectionClosed()` on an 'app started before TWS' launch records nothing, and the first `nextValidId` keeps the reconcile-seeded 1m close), otherwise sets `_outage_active` (its ONLY setter) and `_outage_start.setdefault(symbol, time.time())` for every session with live alarms. Rename `_pause_start` -> `_outage_start` (one ledger, one meaning); `pause_all` keeps its flags and its `setdefault` but no longer sets `_outage_active`; `_start_monitoring`'s staged branch targets the renamed dict. `resume_all` remembers `resuming_from_outage = self._outage_active` at entry, builds gaps from `_outage_start`, clears the ledger and both flags, and sets `session.last_chart_price = None` for EVERY session ONLY when resuming from an outage (a first connect therefore keeps D25.2's cache seed). `MainWindow._on_disconnected` calls `self.alarm_monitor.begin_outage()` as the first statement after `self._ibkr_connected = False`, before the replay-serial bump and before classification; `_on_connected` loses `_resuming_from_pause` and its branch and always runs `reconcile()` then `resume_all()`, reporting `_gaps` when non-empty. THE GATE IS THE SESSION PREDICATE, NOT `MainWindow._ibkr_connected`, AND `_go_live` IS NOT EDITED — `_go_live()` sets only `ib_client._connected`, so a window-flag gate would redden `test_d40_1`-`test_d40_4`, whose `reconcile()` calls all precede their drops. The three stated residuals (a poll-detected drop that recovers on the first attempt, a late `disconnected`, an alarm-CRUD session created before the first handshake) are ACCEPTED, not fixed here. In `tests/test_d40_tws_lifecycle.py`: exactly ONE named re-baseline (`test_d40_4_transient_drop_no_pause_ui`, citing AC-D98.1 and FI-P29-1) and FOUR renames whose assertion content is unchanged (`:199`, `:364`, `:375`, `:402`); the FIFTH read at `:445` is inside the re-baselined case and CHANGES VALUE — `SYM_A` IS in `_outage_start` at the drop, cleared after the resume. Add the new suite `tests/test_d98_outage_baseline.py`. G6 is owner-run and is NEVER claimed by this wave: no case asserts a live TWS socket drop or a live alarm fire; the new suite's docstring says so and names what it proxies.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a session with a live alarm at the drop, When the transport drops and later reconnects — for BOTH classifications (transient, `last_disconnect_class is None`; and TWS_GONE) — Then the symbol is recorded in `_outage_start` at drop time, `_outage_active` is True, the first post-reconnect tick neither evaluates nor fires (`session.last_chart_price is None`), the status line contains `unmonitored` and the symbol, and the pause UI stays TWS-gone-only (on the transient path: `_tws_paused` False, `is_paused` False, `monitoring_paused` False, red badge).

Given the seed tick above, When further ticks arrive on both classifications, Then a tick at or below the level does not fire and the next tick strictly beyond the level fires exactly once — the phase's final crossing rule, after the seed.

Given no session at the drop, When a pre-handshake `connectionClosed()` is followed by a successful `nextValidId(1)`, Then nothing is recorded (`_outage_active` False, `_outage_start == {}`, no `unmonitored` line) and the reconcile-created monitor's `last_chart_price` EQUALS the cached 1m close (no resume-wipe).

Given the one ledger, Then two drops without a successful connect keep the EARLIEST start (`setdefault`), a resume clears both `_outage_start` and `_outage_active`, `begin_outage` is the only setter of `_outage_active` (a `pause_all()` alone leaves it False and a following `resume_all()` changes no baseline), and `_pause_start` no longer exists as an attribute or as a source occurrence in `services/alarm_monitor.py`, `ui/main_window.py` or `tests/test_d40_tws_lifecycle.py`.

Given a symbol with no live alarm, Then a drop produces no ledger entry and no line; given a session created DURING a recorded outage, Then it is re-seeded at resume; and when NO session existed at the drop, Then there is no outage to resume and a session created afterwards keeps its own seed.

Given a second `nextValidId(1)` with no intervening drop, Then every baseline is untouched; given a `begin_outage()` delivered AFTER a resume, Then it arms exactly one re-seed (and one interval line) at the FOLLOWING connect, which `resume_all()` consumes.

Given `tests/test_d40_tws_lifecycle.py`, Then the only behavioural change is the one named re-baseline plus the four `_pause_start` -> `_outage_start` renames, and the only value change is `:445` (`SYM_A` present at the drop, cleared after resume); every other assertion (no TWS_GONE classification, no paused badge, `_tws_paused` False, `is_paused` False, `monitoring_paused` False) is unchanged.

tasks.title: P29-04 — D99: one delivery path per page-ready transition
tasks.description: A page-ready transition delivers from `_op_log` and from nothing else: the staging buffers are DISCARDED, not drained. `set_ready(self, ready: bool)` becomes a flag setter — its `_queued` drain block is deleted and its docstring says a readiness TRANSITION is `handle_page_ready`'s job and this method emits nothing. `handle_page_ready` clears `_queued`, `_outbox` and `_live_buf`, calls `set_ready(True)`, then runs the existing `if self._op_log:` block verbatim (one envelope `{v: 1, ops: list(_op_log)}`, `_emit`, counters, `replayFinished`) and `self._replay_channels()`; the `pending = self.flush()` line and the `envelopes` list go, and it returns the replay envelope or `None` when the log is empty. State the contract once in the module docstring: the log is the single full-state source; a transition delivers each accepted op at most once; a queued op is subsumed by the log, never emitted beside it. Update the `pageReady()` table row from '(drain + replay)' to '(replay)' and its docstring to 'the page's QWebChannel half is subscribed; replay the full log now', and change `ui/lwc_host.py`'s one comment from 'drain + replay' to 'replay' — the `loadFinished` ordering guard and its `set_ready(False)` are untouched. Re-baseline exactly ONE named case in `tests/test_lwc_bridge.py` (`TestBatchShape::test_queue_until_ready_holds_pre_ready_ops`: replace `b.set_ready(True); env = b.flush()` with `env = b.handle_page_ready()` and assert the same two ops arrive once) and add the new suite `tests/test_d99_page_ready_delivery.py`. Do not change `ENVELOPE_VERSION`, the op shapes, `_check_op_shape`, `flush`'s coalescing/replace/directive rules, the counter names, `send_ops`'s log-before-queue order, the channel path, or `handle_render_terminated`; never clear or truncate `_op_log`; add no second envelope per transition, no chunking, no new signal, and no call from `loadFinished`. **Exit condition — the webengine exclusion:** the command above runs with `-m 'not webengine'` because `tests/test_lwc_bridge.py` also holds three `@pytest.mark.webengine` host cases (`test_host_loads_ndt_chart_offline`, `test_render_terminated_recovery_wired`, `test_interceptor_wired_blocks_non_ndt`) that construct a `QWebEnginePage`; on this macOS box that construction aborts with SIGABRT because the harness builds `QApplication([])` — a pre-existing environment limitation, not a D99 regression (evidence: the same abort reproduces with both changed files restored to `HEAD`, and a minimal probe constructs the page fine under `QApplication(sys.argv)`). The pipeline's standard invocation excludes the marker-gated cases; this task's D99 gate is the new suite plus every non-gated bridge case, all green. The gated cases stay the owner's manual-checklist counterparts (DG88/AP-P6-4) — do not add a skip, rewrite the harness, or touch them in this task. The same marker exclusion covers the exit condition's nine companion suites: `tests/test_lwc_bridge_handshake.py` also carries two gated handshake cases (`test_page_bridge_handshake_reaches_window`, `test_view_cycles_keep_page_loads_alive`), so run those nine with `-m 'not webengine'` too — the suites themselves stay unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given N ops accepted while the page is not ready, When the page signals ready once, Then the envelopes emitted in that transition contain each queued op exactly once (multiset over (op, series, ts); duplicate count 0) and the reconstruction equals the expected series.

Given a subsequent render-process recovery (`handle_render_terminated()` then a page-ready transition), Then one envelope carries the full log once, no envelope contains an op twice, the reconstruction equals the expected series, and a second recovery produces the same — the log is never cleared.

Given `_queued` non-empty and the page not ready, When `set_ready(True)` is called, Then emits NOTHING (no envelope, no signal, no counter emission), and the queued ops are delivered exactly once by the next `handle_page_ready()`; `handle_page_ready` returns `None` and increments `replays` once when the log is empty, and one envelope when it is not.

Given the channel path and a live op staged while ready but not yet flushed, When a transition runs, Then the channel queue is dropped and each channel op is replayed once (`_channel_queue` empty), the staged live op crosses exactly once via the log, and a mixed transition yields one bar envelope with each bar op once plus one channel envelope with the channel op once.

tests.expected_result: Each queued op's identity appears exactly once across the transition's envelopes; duplicate count 0; reconstruction equals the expected series; `counters()['queued'] == 5`.

contracts.signature: def set_ready(self, ready: bool) -> None:  # sets self._ready only; emits nothing; no _queued drain

def handle_page_ready(self):  # clear _queued/_outbox/_live_buf; set_ready(True); if _op_log: emit {"v": 1, "ops": list(_op_log)} once (emitted/replays counters + replayFinished); then _replay_channels(); return that envelope, else None; never calls flush()
